subject.title: Feature Request: Support YAML as config file format

question: Should OpenClaw add `.yaml`/`.yml` as supported core config files, or keep JSON5 `openclaw.json` plus `openclaw config` and `config.patch` as the only core config-file contract?
rationale: This changes a compatibility-sensitive config-file contract, and the issue discussion shows a narrower existing mutation path may solve the practical pain without adding a second format.

options.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
options.body: Reaffirm `openclaw.json` as the only core config file and improve docs or prompts around `openclaw config` and `config.patch` for comment-safe scripted edits.

options.title: Approve YAML Contract
options.body: Require a design or PR that defines YAML precedence, parser semantics, write-back behavior, reload handling, doctor coverage, docs, and upgrade validation.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: If maintainers decide the added format surface is not worth the benefit, close this with the CLI/RPC mutation path as the supported alternative.

recommendation.title: Keep JSON5 Canonical
recommendation.body: Reaffirm `openclaw.json` as the only core config file and improve docs or prompts around `openclaw config` and `config.patch` for comment-safe scripted edits.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on config policy/docs and config IO behavior, which makes them the best available product-decision owner.
